sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not a smooth line: operating margin fell 11.9pp to 8.1% in FY2019, then jumped 14.0pp to 22.1% in FY2020 [F23][F24][D109][D160].

The FY2019 collapse came from a $6.8 billion goodwill impairment and a $1.6 billion intangible impairment on Shave Care, driven by currency devaluations, slowing category growth and tougher competition [X109][P62].
FY2020's rebound was mostly the absence of that $8.3 billion base-period charge, with the remaining $1.9 billion from higher sales and gross margin [P71].
Revenue has grown at a 2.0% three-year CAGR from FY2023 to FY2026, and operating margin of 22.7% in FY2026 sits 0.6pp above the 22.1% window median [D664][F30][D648].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing 4.0pp of FY2020 growth and 2.7pp in FY2023 [D518][D527].
In FY2026 the pattern flipped: non-US contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% growth while the US added just 0.1pp [D511][D536][D457].
FY2026 net sales rose on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and contributed 0.8pp in FY2026, while Beauty added 1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D541][D543][D603][D602].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 4.1% CAGR against 3.3%, but in FY2026 it fell 3.4% as revenue rose 3.3% [F202][F201][D458][D457].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits 0.6pp above the window median of 22.1% and well above the FY2019 low of 8.1% [F30][D648][D646].
The 1.6pp margin decline in FY2026 came from a lower gross margin and higher marketing spending, with cost of revenue adding 1.0pp of drag and SG&A 0.6pp [D470][D483][D485][P25].
Gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix, partly offset by lower commodity costs and productivity savings [P5].
Net margin of 18.4% trails operating margin by 4.3pp, reflecting interest and a 20.8% effective tax rate [F50][F30][D693][D443].
Other non-operating income rose $922 million to $1.1 billion on the Glad joint-venture dissolution gain and the prior-year Argentina charge [X108][P24].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, against a window median of 1.25x [F80][F40][D444][D683].
Free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x net income and a 17.4% margin, versus a 17.2% window median [F100][D445][D441][D654].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as working capital added $29 million, with payables generating $919 million partly offset by $641 million consumed by inventory [P3].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F90][D464][D440][D446].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, or 27.8% of revenue, with $9.9 billion of cash against $34.1 billion of debt [D450][D451][D448][D449].
That net-debt ratio ranks at the 67th percentile of three staples peers, whose median net cash position is a net debt of 32.3% of revenue [D694][D695].
Buybacks plus dividends of $15.3 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, after 116.6% in FY2025 [D452][D453][D402].
The diluted share count fell 1.3% in FY2026 and 11.6% from 2,740.4 million in FY2017, helping EPS outgrow net income [D476][X115][X124].
The current ratio is 0.68x in FY2026, below 1.0x and near the window low of 0.63x [F180][D661].
This is structural for a consumer-staples business funded by supplier payables and short-term paper, so it is a liquidity watch item rather than a solvency concern [F180].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% [D402][D453].
Payout above free cash flow is covered by the balance sheet for now, but it leaves little room if capex keeps rising [D453][D446].
Operating margin: a FY2027 print below the 22.1% window median would confirm the FY2026 reversal, while a return above the 24.3% FY2025 high would restore the prior trend [D648][D647].
Capex: a ratio above the FY2026 1.40x of D&A would extend the capital-intensity climb and pressure free cash flow [D446].
Payout: buybacks plus dividends above the FY2026 100.7% of free cash flow would mean further balance-sheet funding of returns [D453].
